verses.21:7: And it was evil in the sight of God concerning this matter, and He struck Israel.
verses.21:8: And David said to God, "I have sinned greatly, because I have done this thing; and now, take away, I pray, the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
verses.21:9: And the Lord spoke to Gad the seer,
verses.21:10: "Go and speak to David, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: Three things I lift up against you; choose for yourself one of them, and I shall do it to you.'"
verses.21:11: And Gad came to David and said to him, "Thus says the Lord: 'Choose for yourself
verses.21:12: either three years of famine, or three months to flee from before your enemies, with the sword of your enemies to destroy, or three days of the sword of the Lord and pestilence in the land, with the angel of the Lord destroying throughout all the inheritance of Israel.' And now, see what I shall answer Him who sent the word."
verses.21:13: And David said to Gad, "All three are exceedingly grievous to me; let me fall now into the hands of the Lord, for His mercies are exceedingly great, and let me by no means fall into the hands of men."
verses.21:14: And the Lord sent pestilence in Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.
verses.21:15: And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. And as he was destroying, the Lord saw and relented concerning the calamity, and said to the destroying angel, "Let it be enough for you; stay your hand." And the angel of the Lord was standing at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
verses.21:16: And David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the Lord standing between the earth and heaven, with his sword drawn in his hand, stretched out over Jerusalem; and David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.
verses.21:17: And David said to God, "Was it not I who commanded to number the people? And I am the one who has sinned, and I have indeed done wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? O Lord God, let Your hand be upon me and upon the house of my father, and not upon Your people for destruction, O Lord."
verses.21:18: And the angel of the Lord spoke to Gad to tell David that he should go up to erect an altar to the Lord at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
verses.21:19: And David went up according to the word of Gad, which he had spoken in the name of the Lord.
verses.21:20: And Orna turned back and saw the king, and his four sons with him were hiding themselves; now Orna was threshing wheat.
verses.21:21: And David came to Orna, and Orna went out from the threshing floor and bowed down to David with his face to the ground.
verses.21:22: And David said to Orna, "Give me your place of the threshing floor, and I shall build upon it an altar to the Lord; give it to me for its full value in silver, and the plague shall cease from the people."
verses.21:23: And Orna said to David, "Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what is good in his sight; behold, I have given the calves for a burnt offering, and the plow for wood, and the wheat for a sacrifice; I have given it all."
verses.21:24: And King David said to Orna, "No, for I will surely buy it for its full value in silver; for I will by no means take what is yours for the Lord, to offer up a burnt offering without cost to the Lord."
verses.21:25: So David gave to Orna for his place six hundred shekels of gold by weight.
verses.21:26: And David built there an altar to the Lord, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings; and he cried out to the Lord, and He answered him by fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering, and it consumed the burnt offering.
verses.21:27: And the Lord spoke to the angel, and he put the sword back into the sheath.
verses.21:28: At that time, when David saw that He had answered him at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
verses.21:29: Now the tabernacle of the Lord, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offerings were at that time in Bamoth in Gibeon.
verses.21:30: And David was not able to go before it to seek God, for he did not hasten from before the sword of the angel of the Lord.
verses.22:1: And David said, "This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar for burnt offering for Israel."
verses.22:2: And David commanded to gather together all the sojourners in the land of Israel; and he appointed stonecutters to hew dressed stones to build a house for God.
verses.22:3: And David prepared much iron for the nails of the doorways and of the gates and for the hinges, and bronze in abundance; there was no weighing it.
verses.22:4: And cedar timber, there was no number to it; for the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought cedar timber in abundance to David.
verses.22:5: And David said, "Solomon my son is a tender young lad, and the house to be built for the Lord is to be of exceeding greatness, for a name and for glory throughout all the earth; I will make preparation for it." So David made preparation in abundance before his death.
verses.22:6: Then he called Solomon his son, and charged him to build the house for the Lord God of Israel.
verses.22:7: And David said to Solomon, "Child, it was in my soul to build a house to the name of the Lord God.
verses.22:8: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, 'You have shed blood in abundance, and you have made great wars; you shall not build a house to My name, because you have shed much blood upon the earth before Me.
verses.22:9: Behold, a son is born to you; he shall be a man of rest, and I will give him rest from all the enemies round about, for Solomon shall be his name, and I will give peace and quietness upon Israel in his days.
verses.22:10: He shall build a house to My name, and he shall be to Me a son, and I will be to him a father, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom in Israel forever.'
verses.22:11: And now, son, the Lord shall be with you, and He shall grant success, and you shall build a house to the Lord your God, as He has spoken concerning you.
verses.22:12: Only may the Lord give you wisdom and understanding, and strengthen you over Israel, both to keep and to do the law of the Lord your God.
verses.22:13: Then He will grant success, if you are careful to do the statutes and the judgments which the Lord commanded Moses concerning Israel; be courageous and be strong; do not fear, nor be terrified.
verses.22:14: And behold, according to my poverty I have prepared for the house of the Lord one hundred thousand talents of gold, and one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron without weight, for it is in abundance; and timber and stones I have prepared, and add to these.
verses.22:15: And with you add an abundance of those who do work, craftsmen and builders of stone and carpenters of wood, and every wise man in every kind of work,
verses.22:16: in gold, in silver, in bronze, and in iron, without number. Arise and act, and may the Lord be with you."
verses.22:17: And David charged the servants, the rulers of Israel, to help Solomon his son,
verses.22:18: "Is not the Lord with you? And He has given you rest round about, for He has given the inhabitants of the land into your hands, and the land has been subdued before the Lord and before His people.
verses.22:19: Now set your hearts and your souls to seek the Lord your God, and arise and build a sanctuary to your God, to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built to the name of the Lord."
verses.23:1: Now David was old and full of days, and he made his son Solomon king in his place over Israel.
verses.23:2: And he gathered together all the leaders of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites.
verses.23:3: And the Levites were numbered from thirty years old and upward, and their number by their head count came to thirty-eight thousand men:
verses.23:4: of the overseers for the work of the house, twenty-four thousand; and scribes and judges, six thousand;
verses.23:5: and four thousand praising the Lord with the instruments which he made to praise the Lord.
verses.23:6: And David divided them into divisions among the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.23:7: And of Parosom: Edan and Shimei.
verses.23:8: The sons of Edan: the chief Jehiel, and Zetham, and Joel—three in all.
verses.23:9: The sons of Shimei: Alothim, Hieiel, and Haidan, three. These were the chiefs of the fathers' houses of Edan.
verses.23:10: And of the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Ziza, Joash, and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei, four.
verses.23:11: Now Jahath was the chief, and Ziza the second; but Joash and Beriah did not multiply sons, so they became one father's house in one reckoning.
verses.23:12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.
verses.23:13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to be consecrated for the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the Lord, to minister, and to pronounce blessing in His name forever.
verses.23:14: Now as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named in the tribe of Levi.
verses.23:15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
verses.23:16: The sons of Gershom: Shubael the chief.
verses.23:17: And the sons of Eliezer were Rehabiah the chief, and there were no other sons; but the sons of Rehabiah increased exceedingly.
verses.23:18: The sons of Izhar: Shelomoth the chief.
verses.23:19: Of the sons of Hebron: Idoud the chief, Amadiah the second, Uzziel the third, and Ikemias the fourth.
verses.23:20: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
verses.23:21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
verses.23:22: And Eleazar died, and he had no sons, only daughters; and the sons of Kish, their brethren, took them.
verses.23:23: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Aidath, and Areimoth, three.
verses.23:24: These were the sons of Levi according to their fathers' houses—the chiefs of their fathers' houses according to their reckoning, by the number of their names, by their head count—who did the work of the ministry of the house of the Lord, from twenty years old and upward.
verses.23:25: For David said, "The Lord God of Israel has given rest to His people, and He has taken up His dwelling in Jerusalem forever."
verses.23:26: And the Levites were not carrying the tabernacle and all its vessels for its ministry;
verses.23:27: for in the last words of David is the number of the sons of Levi from twenty years old and upward,
verses.23:28: because he stationed them at the hand of Aaron to minister in the house of the Lord—over the courts and over the chambers, and over the purification of all the holy things, and over the work of the ministry of God:
verses.23:29: for the showbread, for the fine flour of the sacrifice, and for the unleavened wafers, and for the griddle, and for that which is mixed, and for every measure;
verses.23:30: and to stand in the morning to praise and give thanks to the Lord, and likewise in the evening;
verses.23:31: and over all the burnt offerings offered up to the Lord on the Sabbaths, and on the new moons, and at the feasts, by number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually to the Lord.
verses.23:32: And they shall keep the charges of the tabernacle of witness and the charges of the sons of Aaron their brethren, to minister in the house of the Lord.
verses.24:1: And as for the sons of Aaron by division: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
verses.24:2: And Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons; therefore Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron, served as priests.
verses.24:3: And David divided them, together with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, according to their appointment, according to their ministry, according to their fathers' houses.
verses.24:4: And the sons of Eleazar were found to be more numerous as chiefs of the mighty men than the sons of Ithamar; and he divided them: for the sons of Eleazar, sixteen chiefs for fathers' houses, and for the sons of Aaron, Ithamar, according to fathers' houses.
verses.24:5: And he divided them by lot, one with another; for there were leaders of the sanctuary and leaders of the Lord both among the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar.
verses.24:6: And Shemaiah the son of Nethanel, the scribe of Levi, recorded them before the king and the leaders, and Zadok the priest, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the chiefs of the fathers' houses of the priests and of the Levites—one father's house each for Eleazar, and one each for Ithamar.
verses.24:7: Now the first lot came out for Jarim, the second for Anaideia,
verses.24:8: the third for Hareb, the fourth for Seorim,
verses.24:9: the fifth for Malchijah, the sixth for Benjamin,
verses.24:10: the seventh for Koz, the eighth for Abijah,
verses.24:11: the ninth for Jeshua, the tenth for Shecaniah,
verses.24:12: the eleventh for Eliabiei, the twelfth for Jakim,
verses.24:13: the thirteenth for Ochchopha, the fourteenth for Gelba,
verses.24:14: the fifteenth for Immer, the sixteenth for Chezin,
verses.24:15: the seventeenth for Aphese, the eighteenth for Pethahiah,
verses.24:16: the nineteenth for Ezekiel, the twentieth for Achim,
verses.24:17: the twenty-first for Gamul, the twenty-second for Adallai,
verses.24:19: This was their appointment according to their ministry, to enter into the house of the Lord according to their ordinance by the hand of Aaron their father, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
verses.24:20: And as for the remaining sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Jobael and Jadeiah;
verses.24:22: And of the Izharite, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Inath.
verses.24:23: The sons of Jedeimou: Amadiah the second, Jase the third, Jokom the fourth.
verses.24:24: Of Uzziel, Micah; the sons of Micah, Shamir.
verses.24:25: The brother of Micah, Isshiah; the son of Isshiah, Zechariah.
verses.24:26: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Ozeia:
verses.24:27: of Merari, through Ozeia, his sons were Isoam, Zaccur, and Abai.
verses.24:28: For Mahli: Eleazar and Ithamar; and Eleazar died, and he had no sons.
verses.24:29: For Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
verses.24:30: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, Ela, and Areimoth. These were the sons of the Levites according to their fathers' houses.
verses.24:31: And they also drew lots, just as their brethren the sons of Aaron, before the king, and Zadok, and Ahimelech, and the chief of the fathers' houses of the priests and of the Levites—the patriarchs of Araab, just as his younger brethren.
verses.25:1: And King David and the captains of the army appointed for the service the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who spoke forth with harps, with lutes, and with cymbals; and their number was reckoned head by head of those who labored in their works.
verses.25:2: The sons of Asaph: Sacchus, Joseph, Nathalias, and Erael—sons of Asaph next to the king.
verses.25:3: Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Tuna, Surei, Saia, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattathias, six, after their father Jeduthun, who struck up on the harp thanksgiving and praise to the Lord.
verses.25:4: Of Hemani, the sons of Heman: Bukkias, Manthanias, Azarael, Subael, Amsu, Jeremoth, Hananiah, Eliathath, Godollathi, and Romi; the sons of Od, and Jeibasaka, Manthi, Hothiri, and Melzoth.
verses.25:5: All these were sons to Heman, who played for the king in the words of God, to exalt the horn; and God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
verses.25:6: All these were with their father singing hymns in the house of God with cymbals, with lutes, and with harps, next to the king, together with Asaph, Jeduthun, and Hemani.
verses.25:7: And their number, along with their brethren who were instructed to sing to the Lord, every one who was skillful, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
verses.25:8: And they also cast lots for their courses, both the small and the great, the accomplished and the learners.
verses.25:9: And the first lot of his sons and his brethren came forth for Asaph, to Joseph; Galuia the second, Heneia, his brethren and his sons, twelve;
verses.25:10: the third, Zacchuth, his son and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:11: the fourth, Jesdri, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:12: the fifth, Nathan, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:13: the sixth, Bukkias, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:14: the seventh, Iseriel, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:15: the eighth, Joseia, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:16: the ninth, Manthanias, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:17: the tenth, Emei, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:18: the eleventh, Azariah, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:19: the twelfth, Haria, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:20: the thirteenth, Subael, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:21: the fourteenth, Mattathias, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:22: the fifteenth, Ereimoth, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:23: the sixteenth, Hananiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:24: the seventeenth, Bakata, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:25: the eighteenth, Ananias, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:26: the nineteenth, Methathi, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:27: the twentieth, Aematha, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:28: the twenty-first, Hethi, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:29: the twenty-second, Godomathi, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:30: the twenty-third, Meazoth, his sons and his brethren, twelve;
verses.25:31: the twenty-fourth, Romelchi, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.26:1: For the divisions of the gates, the sons of the Korahites: Mosolael the son of Kore; from the sons of Abia, Saphar.
verses.26:2: And of Mosalea the son of Zechariah, the firstborn was Iderel, Zechariah, Jenonel,
verses.26:3: Jolam, Jonah, and Elionais the seventh.
verses.26:4: And to Obed-Edom were sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jozabath, Joath, Sochar, Naas, Jeiel,
verses.26:5: Ammiel, Issachar, and Japhthoslaathi, for God blessed him.
verses.26:6: And to Shemaiah his son were born sons of the firstborn Rosai to his father's house, for they were mighty men.
verses.26:7: The sons of Shemaiah: Gooni, Raphael, Obed, Elezabath, and Achiud—mighty sons—Ennu, Sabchia, and Isbakom.
verses.26:8: All these were of the sons of Obed-Edom, they and their brethren and their sons, laboring mightily in the work—all of them sixty-two belonging to Obed-Edom.
verses.26:9: And to Mosomamid were sons and brethren, eighteen mighty men.
verses.26:10: And to Hosah, of the sons of Merari, were sons guarding the office, for he was not the firstborn; and his father made him chief of the second division.
verses.26:11: Tablai the third, Zechariah; all these, the sons and brethren of Hosah, were thirteen.
verses.26:12: To these belonged the divisions of the gates, to the chiefs of the mighty men, having courses just as their brethren, to minister in the house of the Lord.
verses.26:13: And they cast lots, both the small and the great, according to their fathers' houses, for each gate.
verses.26:14: And the lot for those toward the east fell to Salameia and Zechariah, sons of Soaz; for Melchia they cast lots, and the lot came forth for the north;
verses.26:15: to Obed-Edom, the south, opposite the house of Esephin;
verses.26:16: for the second, to Hosah toward the west, beyond the gate of the chamber of the ascent—watch opposite watch.
verses.26:17: Toward the east were six a day, on the north four a day, on the south four a day, and at Esephin two
verses.26:18: as reliefs, and for Hosah toward the west, beyond the gate of the chamber, three. Watch opposite watch of the ascent: toward the east six a day, and on the north four, and on the south four, and at Esephim two as reliefs, and toward the west four, and on the pathway two as reliefs.
verses.26:19: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers for the sons of Kohath and for those of Merari.
verses.26:20: And the Levites their brethren were over the treasuries of the house of the Lord and over the treasuries of the consecrated things.
verses.26:21: These were the sons of Chadan, the Gershonite: to Ladan and Jaieel of Jou; the sons of Jeiel were chiefs of the fathers' houses of Ladan; to the Gershonite, Jeiel.
verses.26:22: The sons of Jeiel: Zethom and Joel the brothers were over the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
verses.26:23: Of Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel:
verses.26:24: And Joel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was over the treasuries.
verses.26:25: And to his brother Eliezer was Rehabiah his son, and Osaiah, and Joram, and Zichri, and Shelomoth.
verses.26:26: This Shelomoth and his brethren were over all the treasuries of the holy things, which King David and the chiefs of the fathers' houses, the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and the leaders of the army had consecrated,
verses.26:27: which he took from the cities and from the spoils, and consecrated from them so that the building of the house of God might not be delayed;
verses.26:28: and over all the holy things of God—of Samuel the prophet, and of Saul the son of Kish, and of Abner the son of Ner, and of Joab the son of Zeruiah—all that he consecrated was under the hand of Shelomoth and his brethren.
verses.26:29: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and sons were for the outward work over Israel, to serve as scribes and to judge.
verses.26:30: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, mighty men, one thousand seven hundred, were over the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan toward the west, for every ministry of the Lord and work of the king.
verses.26:31: Of the Hebronites, Tudeias was the chief of the Hebronites, according to their generations, according to their fathers' houses. In the fortieth year of his reign they were sought out, and a mighty man was found among them in Riazer of Gilead.
verses.26:32: And his brethren, mighty sons, were two thousand seven hundred chiefs of the fathers' houses; and King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for every ordinance of the Lord and matter of the king.
verses.27:1: Now the sons of Israel according to their number—the rulers of the fathers' houses, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and the scribes who ministered to the people and in every matter of the king according to divisions, in every matter of the one coming in and going out month by month, throughout all the months of the year—each single division had twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:2: And over the first division for the first month was Sobal the son of Zabdiel, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:3: He was from the sons of Perez, ruler of all the commanders of the army for the first month.
verses.27:4: And over the division for the second month was Dodia the Ekchoch, and in his division were twenty-four thousand, commanders of the army.
verses.27:5: The third for the third month was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the priest, the chief, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:6: This Benaiah was mightier than the thirty and was over the thirty, and over his division was Laibazath his son.
verses.27:7: The fourth for the fourth month was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Obadiah his son and the brethren, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:8: The fifth for the fifth month was the leader Salaoth the Esrae, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:9: The sixth for the sixth month was Oduias the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:10: The seventh for the seventh month was Chesles, who was from Phallus, of the sons of Ephraim, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:11: The eighth for the eighth month was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of Zerah, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:12: The ninth for the ninth month was Abiezer from Anathoth, from the land of Benjamin, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:13: The tenth for the tenth month was Maharai, who was from Netophah, of Zerah, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:14: The eleventh for the eleventh month was Benaiah, who was from Pirathon, of the sons of Ephraim, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:15: The twelfth for the twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:16: Now over the tribes of Israel: for those of Reuben, the leader was Eliezer the son of Zichri; for Simeon, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
verses.27:17: for Levi, Hashabiah the son of Samuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
verses.27:18: for Judah, Eliab, one of the brothers of David; for Issachar, Omri the son of Mishael;
verses.27:19: for Zebulun, Shemaiah the son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth the son of Azriel;
verses.27:20: for Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Uzziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Phaladaia;
verses.27:21: for the half-tribe of Manasseh among those in Gilead, Jaddai the son of Zabdiu; for the sons of Benjamin, Asier the son of Abner;
verses.27:22: for Dan, Azarel the son of Joram. These were the patriarchs of the tribes of Israel.
verses.27:23: And David did not take the number of those from twenty years old and under, because the Lord had said He would multiply Israel like the stars of heaven.
verses.27:24: And Joab the son of Zeruiah began to number among the people, but he did not finish; and because of these things wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not recorded in the book of the accounts of the days of King David.
verses.27:25: And over the king's treasuries was Azmaveth the son of Adiel; and over the storehouses in the field, and in the villages, and in the hamlets, and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah.
verses.27:26: And over those who tilled the ground, those who labored, was Ezri the son of Chobud.
verses.27:27: And over the fields was Shimei, who was from Rael; and over the storehouses of wine in the fields was Zachri the son of Sephni.
verses.27:28: And over the olive groves and over the sycamore trees that were in the lowland was Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the storehouses of oil was Joash.
verses.27:29: And over the grazing cattle that were in Asidon was Asartais the Sharonite; and over the cattle that were in the valleys was Sophan the son of Adai.
verses.27:30: And over the camels was Abias the Ishmaelite; and over the donkeys was Jehdeiah, who was from Merathon.
verses.27:31: And over the sheep was Jaziz the Garite. All these were stewards of the possessions of King David.
verses.27:32: Also Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding; and Jehiel the son of Hachami was with the king's sons.
verses.27:33: Ahithophel was the king's counselor, and Hushai was the first friend of the king.
verses.27:34: And next after this Ahithophel were Jehoiada the son of Benaiah and Abiathar; and Joab was the commander-in-chief of the king.
verses.28:1: Now David assembled all the rulers of Israel, the rulers of the judges, and the rulers of the divisions who attended the person of the king, and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the treasurers, and those who were over his possessions, and the mighty men, and the warriors, in Jerusalem.
verses.28:2: And David stood in the midst of the assembly and said, "Hear me, brethren and my people: It came into my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and a footstool for our Lord, and I have prepared the materials needed for the dwelling.
verses.28:3: But God said, 'You shall not build a house for Me to call My name upon it, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.'
verses.28:4: Yet the Lord God of Israel chose me out of all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever; and in Judah He chose the kingdom, and from the house of Judah, the house of my father; and in me He took pleasure, that I should become king over all Israel.
verses.28:5: And of all my sons—for the Lord has given me many sons—He has chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.
verses.28:6: And God said to me, 'Solomon your son shall inherit My house and My court, for I have chosen him to be My son, and I will be a Father to him.
verses.28:7: And I will establish his kingdom forever, if he is steadfast to keep My commandments and My judgments, as it is this day.'
verses.28:8: And now, in the sight of all the assembly of the Lord, seek out the commandments of the Lord our God, that you may inherit the good land for our sons forever.
verses.28:9: And now, Solomon, know the God of your fathers and serve Him with a perfect heart and a willing soul; for the Lord searches all hearts and knows every thought. If you seek Him, He will be found by you; and if you forsake Him, He will forsake you to the end.
verses.28:10: See, therefore: the Lord has chosen you to build a house for Him as a sanctuary; be strong and do it."
verses.28:11: Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the temple, and of its houses, and of its treasuries, and of the upper chambers, and of the inner storehouses, and of the house of atonement,
verses.28:12: and the pattern that he had in his spirit of the courts of the house of the Lord, and of all the chambers round about, for the storehouses of the Lord, and of the storehouses of the holy things,
verses.28:13: and of the quarters of the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the work of the service of the house of the Lord, and of the storehouses of the vessels for service.
verses.28:14: And he gave him the exact weight of them, both of the gold and of the silver, and the weight of the lampstands
verses.28:16: He gave him likewise the weight of the tables of the showbread, for each table of gold, and likewise for those of silver;
verses.28:17: and of the flesh-hooks, and the libation cups, and the bowls of gold, and the weight of those of gold and of silver, for each weight.
verses.28:18: And he showed him the weight of the altar of incense of refined gold, and the pattern of the chariot of the cherubim that spread out their wings and overshadowed the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
verses.28:19: All these things in writing from the hand of the Lord David gave to Solomon, according to the understanding that had come to him concerning the workmanship of the pattern.
verses.28:20: And David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and of good courage, and do it; do not fear nor be dismayed, for the Lord my God is with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you until you have finished all the work for the service of the house of the Lord. The pattern of the temple and of its house and its treasury, and the upper chambers and the inner storehouses and the house of atonement, and the pattern of the house of the Lord.
verses.28:21: And behold, the divisions of the priests and the Levites are for all the service of the house of the Lord; and they are with you in every undertaking, along with every willing man in wisdom for every craft; and the rulers and all the people are ready for all your words."
verses.29:1: And David the king said to all the assembly, "Solomon my son, whom the Lord has chosen, is young and tender, and the work is great, for it is not for man, but for the Lord God.
verses.29:2: With all my strength I have prepared for the house of my God gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, soom stones and stones for setting, and costly and variegated stones, and every precious stone, and Parian marble in abundance.
verses.29:3: Moreover, because I have set my delight on the house of my God, I have gold and silver that I have acquired for myself, and behold, I have given it to the house of my God over and above, apart from what I have prepared for the house of the holy things:
verses.29:4: three thousand talents of gold from Souphir and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay with them the walls of the temple
verses.29:5: by the hand of craftsmen. And who is willing to fill his hands today for the Lord?"
verses.29:6: Then the rulers of the fathers' houses, and the rulers of the sons of Israel, and the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, and the overseers of the works, and the builders of the king offered willingly;
verses.29:7: and they gave for the works of the house of the Lord five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand gold pieces, and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
verses.29:8: And those with whom stones were found gave them to the storehouses of the house of the Lord by the hand of Besiel the Gersomnite.
verses.29:9: Then the people rejoiced because they had offered willingly, for with a full heart they had offered willingly to the Lord; and David the king rejoiced greatly.
verses.29:10: And King David blessed the Lord before the assembly, saying,
verses.29:11: "Blessed are You, O Lord God of Israel, our Father, from everlasting even to everlasting. You, O Lord, are the greatness and the power and the splendor and the victory and the strength, for You exercise dominion over all things in heaven and on earth; before Your presence every king and nation is troubled.
verses.29:12: From You come riches and glory; You rule over all, O Lord, the Ruler of every dominion, and in Your hand are strength and might; and in Your hand, O Almighty, it is to make great and to strengthen all things.
verses.29:13: And now, O Lord, we give thanks to You and praise the name of Your splendor.
verses.29:14: And who am I, and who are Your people, that we have had the strength to offer willingly to You in this manner? For all things belong to You, and from what is Yours we have given to You.
verses.29:15: For we are sojourners before You, and dwellers, as were all our fathers; like a shadow are our days upon the earth, and there is no abiding.
verses.29:16: O Lord our God, as for all this abundance that I have prepared for a house to be built for Your holy name, it is from Your hand, and all things belong to You.
verses.29:17: And I know, O Lord, that You are the One who tests hearts, and You love righteousness. In singleness of heart I have willingly offered all these things; and now I have seen Your people who are found here offering willingly to You with gladness.
verses.29:18: O Lord God of Abraham, and Isaac, and Israel our fathers, preserve these things in the thoughts of the heart of Your people forever, and direct their hearts toward You.
verses.29:19: And to Solomon my son give a good heart to do Your commandments, Your testimonies, and Your ordinances, and to bring to completion the building of Your house."
verses.29:20: Then David said to all the assembly, "Bless the Lord our God." And all the assembly blessed the Lord God of their fathers, and bending their knees, they bowed down before the Lord and the king.
verses.29:21: And David sacrificed sacrifices to the Lord, and offered up burnt offerings to God on the day after the first day: one thousand young bulls, one thousand rams, one thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
verses.29:22: And they ate and drank before the Lord on that day with joy. And they made Solomon the son of David king, and anointed him to the Lord as king, and Zadok to the priesthood.
verses.29:23: And Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father, and he was approved, and all Israel obeyed him.
verses.29:24: The rulers and the mighty men, and the sons of King David his father, submitted themselves to him.
verses.29:25: And the Lord magnified Solomon from above before all Israel; and they gave him the glory of a king such as had not been upon any king before him.
verses.29:26: And David the son of Jesse reigned over Israel
verses.29:27: forty years: in Hebron seven years, in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
verses.29:28: And he died in a good old age, full of days, with riches and glory; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
verses.29:29: Now the rest of the acts of King David, the former and the latter, are written in the words of Samuel the seer, and in the words of Nathan the prophet, and in the words of Gad the seer,
verses.29:30: concerning all his reign and his might, which came to pass upon him, and upon Israel, and upon all the kingdoms of the earth. Solomon the son of David grew strong over his kingdom; and the Lord his God was with him, and exalted him on high.

notes.1:10: The Greek text describes Nimrod as "a giant hunter" (gigas kynegos), echoing Genesis 10:8–9, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads simply "a mighty one."
notes.1:17: Following the shorter Greek manuscript tradition (Codex Vaticanus), verses 11–16 and 17b–23 are absent here, linking Elam and Asshur directly to Arphaxad in verse 24; in verse 5, the Greek also includes Elishah among the sons of Japheth.
notes.1:30: The Greek preserves distinctive proper-name forms here—Mama, Manasseh, and Chondan (with Massa placed in verse 29)—and similarly preserves Jacob before Esau in verse 34 and distinctive Greek forms such as Onan, Elath, Namna, Solam, Shob, Sonan, Balaam, and Zukam in verses 38–42.
notes.1:43: The Greek introduces the Edomite rulers concisely as "their kings" (omitting the reference to kings reigning over Israel) and preserves the Greek name forms Balak here, Barad and Gethaim in verse 46, and Barad and Peor in verse 50.
notes.1:47: Verses 47–51 preserve a textual dislocation found in Codex Vaticanus: verse 47 breaks off mid-sentence, verse 48 introduces Hadda, Samlah, Shaul, and three Edomite chiefs (Teman, Gola, Jethet), verse 49 isolates Baal-Hanan son of Achbor, and verse 54 concludes with Zaphoin (corresponding to Iram in the Hebrew).
notes.2:9: The Septuagint lists four sons of Hezron here, adding Aram alongside Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chabel (Hebrew Chelubai), and in verse 10 traces Amminadab's descent through Arran rather than Ram.
notes.2:18: The Greek literally states that Caleb fathered Gazuba a wife and Elioth, reflecting a literal rendering of the Hebrew construction referring to his wives Azubah and Jerioth.
notes.2:24: Where the Hebrew reads 'in Caleb-ephrathah,' the Septuagint reads a verb and subject, 'Caleb came to Ephrathah.'
notes.2:38: In verses 38 and 47, the Septuagint reads 'Joshua' (Greek Iesous) where the Hebrew text has 'Jehu' and 'Jahdai,' respectively.
notes.2:53: The Septuagint transliterates the Hebrew word for 'families' as the proper name Emospheos and reads 'the cities of Jair' rather than 'Kiriath-jearim,' while verse 55 renders 'families of scribes' literally as 'the families of writings.'
notes.3:1: The Greek reads "the Israelitess" (rather than "the Jezreelitess" of the Hebrew text) and spells David's second son "Damniel" (for "Daniel").
notes.3:4: The Septuagint omits the clause found in the Hebrew text stating that David reigned in Hebron seven years and six months.
notes.3:11: The Greek reads "Uzziah" (Ozeia) where the Hebrew text has "Ahaziah," and similarly reads "Amnon" for "Amon" in verse 14.
notes.3:19: The Septuagint lists Zerubbabel directly as the son of Shealtiel (omitting Pedaiah), matching the genealogy in Ezra 3:2, Haggai 1:1, and Matthew 1:12.
notes.4:5: The Greek reads "Sara" (Σαρά), a masculine name for the father of Tekoa (corresponding to Hebrew "Ashhur"), distinct from the matriarch Sarah.
notes.4:9: The Septuagint spells the name "Igabes" (Hebrew "Jabez") and renders his mother's explanation by transliterating the Hebrew wordplay as "as gabes" rather than translating it as "in pain."
notes.4:10: Where the Hebrew text petitions God to keep him from harm so that it may not cause him pain, the Septuagint reads "grant knowledge so as not to humble me."
notes.4:21: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew phrase for "workers of fine linen" as "ephrath abak," and in verse 22 similarly transliterates "the records are ancient" as "abederein athoukiein."
notes.4:27: The Septuagint counts "three daughters" (rather than "six daughters" as in the Hebrew text) and omits two intermediate generations in verse 26.
notes.4:39: The Greek reads "Gerar" (where the Hebrew text has "Gedor") and treats the Hebrew word for "the valley" as the proper name "Gai."
notes.5:1: The Greek reads "when he went up to his father's bed, he gave his blessing to his son Joseph" rather than the Hebrew "because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph."
notes.5:6: Several Greek personal and place names in this chapter differ from the Hebrew (including Harson, Benaiah, Echa, Recha, Beel, Balec, Sabat, Chima, Obed, Idai, Zabucham, Geriam, Baalim, and Mariel); Thalgabanasar here and Thagnaphamasar in verse 26 (alongside Phaloch for Pul) reflect the Greek forms of Tiglath-Pileser.
notes.5:10: The Greek translates the name of the Hagrites as a common noun, "the sojourners," while retaining "Hagrites" in verses 19–20.
notes.5:13: Although only seven names are listed, the Greek explicitly gives the total as "eight" (the Hebrew reads "seven").
notes.5:21: The Greek reads "five thousand" camels, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "fifty thousand."
notes.6:1: In the Septuagint, chapter 6 begins here (corresponding to Hebrew MT 6:16, as MT 6:1–15 stand at the end of chapter 5); the Greek consistently writes Gedson for Gershon throughout this chapter.
notes.6:8: In 6:6–13 the Greek text preserves several distinct personal names compared with the Hebrew Masoretic Text, including Joab, Adei, Jaara, Haresi, Suphi, Kainath, Kohath (in 6:9), Alimoth, Abiathar, Aseri, Idaer, and Sani.
notes.6:14: The Greek omits "of Merari: Mahli" (found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text at 6:29), beginning the verse literally "The sons: Libni his son."
notes.6:17: The Greek reads "the tabernacle of the house of testimony" (MT: "the tabernacle of the tent of meeting"), "with instruments" (MT: "with singing"), and "the house" (MT: "the house of the Lord").
notes.6:19: In the lineages of the singers (6:19–30), the Greek preserves several distinct name forms compared with the Hebrew Masoretic Text, including Jeroboam, Tohu, Meth, Amathiu, Abiasar, Aziah, Zammam, Etham, and Asebi.
notes.6:37: In the high-priestly lineage (6:36–38), the Greek preserves the distinct name forms Seraiah (MT: Zerahiah), Mariel (MT: Meraioth), and Ahisama (MT: Ahimaaz).
notes.6:42: In 6:42–45 the Greek preserves several distinct city names compared with the Hebrew Masoretic Text, including Selna, Eglam, Gethoron, the additional city Attan (6:44), and Anchoch (6:45).
notes.6:48: The Greek reads "from the tribe of Dan" (Hebrew MT 6:63 reads "from the tribe of Gad"), and in 6:50 lists only Judah and Simeon (omitting Benjamin).
notes.6:54: Compared with the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Greek lists one city in 6:54 (omitting Gath Rimmon) and one in 6:55 (Amar, omitting Bileam), and in 6:56–62 preserves several distinct place-name forms (including Aseroth, Deberi, Dabor, Jethar, Debir, Maasa, Abaran, Hamoth, and Thachia).
notes.6:63: The Greek reads "and Jericho on the west of the Jordan" (Hebrew MT 6:78 reads "by Jericho on the east side of the Jordan"), omits Jahzah, and in 6:64–66 preserves the place-name forms Kadamos, Maephla, Rammon Gilead, Maanaith, and Gazer.
notes.7:6: The Greek reads simply "Benjamin, Abeira, and Adeiel—three," omitting "the sons of" and diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael"). Throughout this chapter, several personal names preserve distinct Septuagint forms (such as Tholaek, Phut, and Jassur in 7:1; Zeirrei in 7:3; and Ariel in 7:10–11).
notes.7:13: The Greek reads "Solomon" and "Balam" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Shallum" and "Bilhah."
notes.7:16: The Greek calls Machir's son "Souros" (Hebrew "Peresh") and passes directly to "his son was Ulam" and "Badam" in 7:17, lacking the intervening clauses found in the Hebrew text.
notes.7:24: The Greek renders the opening clause ("and among those who remained") as a continuation of Ephraim's statement in 7:23 rather than introducing a daughter named Sheerah as in the Hebrew, and it takes "Ozan" and "Seera" as personal names rather than the town Uzzen-sheerah.
notes.7:29: The Greek lists "Thalme" and "Balad" where the Hebrew has "Taanach," and reads singular "in this" (referring to the territory) rather than plural "in these."
notes.8:1: The Greek text names Benjamin's sons Beleleel (called Bela in v. 3), Saba, Japhael, Joa, and Raphe (v. 2), reflecting the Septuagint forms rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Bela, Ashbel, Aharah, Nohah, Rapha).
notes.8:7: The Greek treats Higaam as a personal name and gives his sons as Naana and Jachichol, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a verb ("he removed them") followed by the names Uzza and Ahihud.
notes.8:12: The Greek text records only Onan and its villages, omitting Lod, which appears alongside Ono in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:38: Although the Greek states that Esel had six sons, only five names are listed because the second Hebrew name (Bocheru) is translated as "his firstborn."
notes.8:39: The Greek reads Asel for the name of Esel's brother (Hebrew Masoretic Text: Eshek) and names his sons Elam, Gag, and Eliphaleis (Hebrew: Ulam, Jeush, Eliphelet).
notes.9:2: The Greek reads "the Levite sons, the priests, and the given ones" (οἱ δεδομένοι, the literal Septuagint rendering of the Nethinim, temple servants given to sanctuary service), differing in order from the Hebrew text.
notes.9:19: The Greek names the Korahite leader "Solomon the son of Koreb" rather than the Hebrew "Shallum the son of Kore," and omits "of the Lord" after "the camp."
notes.9:20: The Greek reads "and these were with him" (καὶ οὗτοι μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the Lord was with him."
notes.9:31: The Greek adds "of the high priest" (τοῦ μεγάλου ἱερέως) to the pan-offering supervised by Mattathias, and in 9:32 reads the personal name "Benaiah the Kohathite."
notes.9:44: Although the Greek states that Esel had six sons, only five names follow because the Hebrew name Bocheru was rendered as "his firstborn" (πρωτότοκος αὐτοῦ); similarly, in 9:37 the Hebrew name Ahio is translated as the common noun "a brother" (ἀδελφὸς).
notes.10:1: Throughout this chapter the Septuagint designates the Philistines as "the foreigners" (ἀλλόφυλοι, literally "people of another tribe") and renders the battle casualties as "wounded" (τραυματίαι).
notes.10:3: The Greek shifts to plural pronouns ("found them... they suffered pain") and includes the distinctive phrase "with bows and pains" (ἐν τόξοις καὶ πόνοις).
notes.10:10: The Greek reads plural "their armor" (τὰ σκεύη αὐτῶν) and singular "their god" (θεοῦ αὐτῶν); in 10:11–12 it also reads "Gilead" rather than "Jabesh-gilead" and adds "and to Israel."
notes.10:13: The Septuagint preserves the explicit clause "and Samuel the prophet answered him" (καὶ ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ Σαμουὴλ ὁ προφήτης), which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.11:2: The Greek reads 'the Lord of Israel said to you' (taking indeclinable Israel as genitive), rather than the Hebrew 'the Lord your God said to you.'
notes.11:8: The Greek reads 'and he fought and took the city,' differing markedly from the Hebrew text, which mentions the Millo and Joab repairing the rest of the city.
notes.11:13: Here and throughout this section (vv. 13-18), the Greek uses allophyloi ('foreigners'), the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines.
notes.11:22: The Greek renders 'from Kabzeel' as 'above Kabzeel' (hyper Kabasael) and leaves the Hebrew title ariel ('lionlike heroes') transliterated as 'Ariels.'
notes.11:26: Throughout verses 11-47, the Greek preserves numerous proper names and gentilics that differ substantially from the Hebrew Masoretic Text (such as Jesebada, Phasodome, Chthaod, Bennaias the Somologennunite, and Sele).
notes.12:1: Sokla (spelled Soglam in 12:21) is the Septuagint form corresponding to Ziklag in the Hebrew text.
notes.12:4: In the Greek text, the names that form verse 5 in the Hebrew versification are combined into verse 4.
notes.12:18: The Greek reads "not in truth of hand" and "the God of your fathers," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "though there is no wrong in my hands" and "the God of our fathers."
notes.12:20: "Philistines" translates Greek allophyloi (literally "foreigners"), the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines throughout Chronicles.
notes.12:22: "The Geddur" preserves the Septuagint transliteration of the Hebrew term for a raiding band (ha-gedud) as a proper name.
notes.13:6: The Greek reads "the city of David" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text names Baalah (Kirjath Jearim).
notes.13:7: The Greek reads "Aminadab" and "his brethren," where the Hebrew text reads "Abinadab" and "Ahio."
notes.13:11: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Perez-Uzzah directly as "Breach of Uzzah," preserving the wordplay with "broken out with a breach."
notes.13:13: Abeddara (spelled Abeddaram in 13:14) is the Septuagint form corresponding to Obed-Edom in the Hebrew text.
notes.14:9: "The Valley of the Giants" renders the Septuagint translation of the Hebrew Valley of Rephaim.
notes.14:11: Phaalphathisim and Breach of Pharisin are the Septuagint forms corresponding to Baal-Perazim, translating "Breach" into Greek to reflect David's wordplay.
notes.14:14: "The pear trees" follows the specific Greek reading (apioi), where the Hebrew term (bekha'im) is often rendered "mulberry" or "balsam" trees.
notes.14:16: Gazara is the Septuagint form corresponding to Gezer in the Hebrew text.
notes.15:5: The Greek numbers for the Levitical divisions in verses 5-7 (110, 250, and 150) and several name forms in verses 8-11 (Elisaphat, Ener, Ariel, and Enel) follow the Septuagint text rather than the Hebrew.
notes.15:15: The Greek reads 'according to the writing' (kata ten graphen), reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew term rendered 'on their shoulders' in the Masoretic Text.
notes.15:20: Alamoth (verse 20) and Amasenith (verse 21) are Greek transliterations of ancient Hebrew musical terms; several musician names in verses 18-21 and 24 (including Uzziel, Elioel, Eliphena, Eithel, Enphanaiah, Uzziah, and Somniah) preserve the distinct Greek forms.
notes.15:27: The Greek names Jechoniah rather than Chenaniah as chief of the songs, and describes David as wearing a robe of fine linen rather than a linen ephod.
notes.16:3: The Greek lists two items distributed to each person—a baker's loaf of bread and a sweet cake (amoreites)—rather than the three portions found in the Hebrew text.
notes.16:23: Verse 24 of the traditional numbering is absent from this Greek critical text, which moves directly from verse 23 to verse 25.
notes.16:28: The Greek reads 'the Father of the nations' (patri ton ethnon) rather than 'families of the peoples' as in the Hebrew text.
notes.16:32: The Greek reads 'the tree of the field' (xylon agrou) where the Hebrew text reads 'let the field exult.'
notes.16:39: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for 'high place' as a proper place name, Bama.
notes.17:6: Greek reads 'any one tribe' (phyle), agreeing with 2 Samuel 7:7, where the Hebrew text of 1 Chronicles reads 'judges.'
notes.17:10: Greek reads 'I will increase you, and the Lord will build you up,' where the Hebrew text reads 'I tell you that the Lord will build you a house.'
notes.17:16: Greek reads 'that You have loved me forever,' whereas the Hebrew text reads 'that You have brought me thus far.'
notes.17:23: In verses 23-24, the Greek text is shorter than the Hebrew, moving directly from 'be confirmed forever' to 'as men say.'
notes.18:1: Here and in verse 11, 'Philistines' renders Greek allophyloi (literally 'foreigners'), the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines.
notes.18:7: Greek reads 'golden collars' (kloious), where the Hebrew text reads 'shields of gold.'
notes.18:8: Greek reads 'Metabechas' (for Hebrew 'Tibhath') and 'choice wars' (eklekton polemon), likely an early scribal shift from 'choice cities' (poleon), where the Hebrew text reads 'Chun.'
notes.18:15: In verses 15-16, the Greek text reads 'Ahijah' (for Hebrew 'Ahilud') and 'Joshua' (Greek Iesous, for Hebrew 'Shavsha').
notes.18:17: Greek reads 'over the priests and Phalteia,' corresponding to the Hebrew text's 'over the Cherethites and the Pelethites.'
notes.19:2: Greek reads 'Hanan the son of Hanas' (and omits the father's name in verse 1), corresponding to Hebrew 'Hanun the son of Nahash.'
notes.19:6: Greek reads 'that the people of David had been put to shame' (Hebrew: 'that they had made themselves odious to David') and 'Sobal' (Hebrew: 'Zobah').
notes.19:13: The Greek text preserves a shorter ending to Joab's speech than the Hebrew, omitting his exhortation to be strong for the people and cities of God.
notes.19:16: Greek names Hadarezer's commander 'Shophar' here and 'Shaphath' in verse 18, both corresponding to Hebrew 'Shophach.'
notes.20:2: The Septuagint reads the proper name Molchol ("Molchol their king"), where the Hebrew text is variously read as Milcom or "their king," and has singular "a precious stone."
notes.20:3: "To the servants, the sons of Ammon" renders Greek tois paisin huiois Ammon, likely an early scribal variant for pasin ("all"), whereas the Hebrew reads "all the cities of the sons of Ammon."
notes.20:4: "Foreigners" translates Greek allophylon, the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines; verses 4-5 also preserve the distinct Septuagint names Sobochai the Thosathite, Saphut, Ellan, and Elemee.
notes.20:8: The Septuagint explicitly states "all of them were four giants," a clause absent from the Masoretic Text of 1 Chronicles 20:8 though paralleling 2 Samuel 21:22.
notes.21:1: Greek diabolos (without the article) denotes "the devil" or "an adversary," rendering Hebrew satan.
notes.21:4: The Septuagint verse is brief, omitting the account of Joab's circuit through Israel found in the Hebrew text, while placing the statement that the king's word prevailed over Joab in verse 6.
notes.21:5: The Septuagint gives only Israel's muster of one million one hundred thousand men and omits the separate count for Judah found in the Hebrew text.
notes.21:20: The Septuagint reads "the king" rather than "the angel," and transliterates the Hebrew participle meaning "hiding themselves" as methachabein; throughout verses 15-28 it also renders the Jebusite's name as Orna (Hebrew Ornan).
notes.21:29: Greek en Bamoth en Gabaon transliterates the Hebrew term for "the high place" as the place name Bamoth; in verse 30, Greek ou katespeusen ("did not hasten") also differs from the Hebrew ("was terrified").
notes.22:14: "According to my poverty" translates Greek kata ten ptocheian mou, reflecting the Septuagint's understanding of Hebrew be-onyi ("in my affliction/trouble").
notes.22:15: The Septuagint includes the imperative "add" (prosthes) in this verse, echoing the closing verb of verse 14.
notes.22:17: "The servants, the rulers of Israel" renders Greek tois paisin archousin Israel, likely an early scribal variant for pasin ("all"), as in 20:3.
notes.23:5: The Greek text omits the four thousand gatekeepers found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, leaving thirty-four thousand itemized out of the thirty-eight thousand total in verse 3.
notes.23:7: Greek Parosom and Edan correspond to the Gershonites and Ladan in the Hebrew text; several personal names in verses 9, 19, and 23 also preserve distinct Septuagint forms (including Alothim, Hieiel, Haidan, Idoud, Amadiah, Ikemias, Aidath, and Areimoth).
notes.23:32: The Greek text names two charges—the tabernacle of witness and the sons of Aaron—without the additional clause concerning the charge of the holy place found in the Hebrew text.
notes.24:4: The Greek text reads "chiefs of the mighty men" and closes with "for the sons of Aaron, Ithamar, according to fathers' houses," omitting the number eight found in the Hebrew text.
notes.24:9: Greek Benjamin corresponds to Mijamin in the Hebrew text; several other priestly course names in verses 7-18 (including Jarim, Anaideia, Hareb, Eliabiei, Ochchopha, Gelba, Chezin, Aphese, Achim, Adallai, and Maasai) likewise preserve distinct Septuagint forms.
notes.24:18: The Greek text concludes the priestly courses at the twenty-third lot rather than the twenty-fourth, as one course is absent earlier in the list, shifting the numbering from the fourteenth lot onward.
notes.24:28: The Greek text uniquely adds "and Ithamar" as a son of Mahli and states that Eleazar died; verses 20-27 and 30 also preserve condensed clauses and distinct Septuagint forms (including Jobael, Inath, Jedeimou, Jase, Jokom, Ozeia, Isoam, Abai, and Ela).
notes.24:31: Greek Araab reflects a transliteration of the Hebrew word for "head" or "chief," yielding "the patriarchs of Araab" in the Septuagint text.
notes.25:3: The Greek text names all six sons of Jeduthun (including Shimei) to match the stated total of six, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text names only five; the forms Tuna, Surei, and Saia also differ from the Hebrew.
notes.25:4: The Greek list of Heman's sons includes Amsu and divides the Hebrew name Romamti-Ezer into "Romi; the sons of Od," preserving a distinct Septuagint transmission of these names.
notes.25:5: The Greek reads "who played for the king" (literally, striking up music), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes Heman as "the king's seer."
notes.25:9: The Greek inserts "Heneia" after "Galouia the second" (likely from a Hebrew pronoun read as a proper name); throughout verses 9–31, several lot names such as Nathan, Emei, Haria, and Bakata reflect distinctive Septuagint forms.
notes.26:1: The Greek divides the ancestral name Ebiasaph/Abiasaph into "from the sons of Abia, Saphar," and reads "divisions of the gates" (as also in verse 12) rather than "gatekeepers."
notes.26:6: The Greek reads "of the firstborn Rosai," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes Shemaiah's sons as rulers over their father's house.
notes.26:10: The Greek renders the Hebrew name "Shimri the chief" as "sons guarding the office" and attaches "of the second division" to verse 10, omitting Hilkiah at the start of verse 11.
notes.26:18: "Esephin" (verses 15, 17) and "Esephim" (verse 18) transliterate the Hebrew term for the storehouse (Asuppim); the Greek text of verse 18 also contains an expanded repetition of the guard postings from verses 16–17.
notes.26:27: The Greek reads "from the cities" (rather than "from the battles") and "so that the building of the house of God might not be delayed" (rather than "to maintain the house of the Lord"); verses 20, 24, and 31 likewise preserve distinctive Septuagint readings ("the Levites their brethren," "Joel," and "Tudeias ... in Riazer").
notes.27:1: The Greek reads "who ministered to the people" (τῷ λαῷ), whereas the Hebrew text reads "who served the king."
notes.27:2: The Septuagint preserves several distinct proper names throughout this chapter—including Sobal (v. 2), Dodia the Ekchoch (v. 4), Laibazath (v. 6), Obadiah (v. 7), Salaoth the Esrae (v. 8), Oduias (v. 9), Chesles from Phallus (v. 10), Samuel (v. 17), Mishael (v. 18), Phaladaia (v. 20), Jaddai son of Zabdiu and Asier (v. 21), Chobud (v. 26), Rael and Zachri son of Sephni (v. 27), Asidon, Asartais, and Sophan son of Adai (v. 29), Abias (v. 30), and the Garite (v. 31)—which differ from the Masoretic Hebrew forms.
notes.27:7: The Greek reads "Obadiah" (Ἀβδείας) rather than "Zebadiah" and "and the brethren" (καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants rendered "after him" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.27:27: The Greek has "fields" (χωρίων) in both clauses rather than "vineyards" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.27:33: The Greek renders Hushai's title as "the first friend of the king" (ὁ πρῶτος φίλος τοῦ βασιλέως), a recognized Hellenistic royal court rank, rather than "the Archite, the king's friend."
notes.28:1: The Greek reads "the rulers of the judges" (ἄρχοντας τῶν κριτῶν) where the Hebrew text has "the officials of the tribes."
notes.28:6: The Greek reads "shall inherit My house and My court" (κληρονομήσει... τὴν αὐλήν μου), whereas the Hebrew text reads "shall build My house and My courts."
notes.28:11: "Its treasuries" renders the Septuagint transliteration ζακχώ (and σακχώ in v. 20), derived from a Semitic term for treasuries or storerooms; the Greek also reads "of the temple" (τοῦ ναοῦ) where the Hebrew has "of the vestibule."
notes.28:14: Verses 14 and 15 are substantially shorter in the Greek text than in the Masoretic Hebrew, omitting the detailed repetitions of the weights for the individual vessels and lampstands.
notes.28:20: The concluding sentence of this verse ("The pattern of the temple... house of the Lord.") is a Septuagint doublet repeating elements from verses 11 and 12 within David's closing charge to Solomon.
notes.29:2: Greek "soom stones" transliterates the Hebrew gem name shoham (commonly identified as onyx), and Greek "parion" specifically designates Parian marble.
notes.29:4: Greek reads "Souphir," the characteristic Septuagint form of the place name corresponding to Ophir in the Hebrew text.
notes.29:8: Greek reads "Besiel the Gersomnite," differing from the Hebrew text's Jehiel the Gershonite.
notes.29:11: Greek uses the nominative "You, O Lord" and concludes with the distinctive Septuagint clause "before Your presence every king and nation is troubled," in place of the Hebrew "Yours is the kingdom, O LORD, and You are exalted as head over all."
notes.29:30: The final sentence ("Solomon the son of David grew strong...") is a Septuagint reading that anticipates 2 Chronicles 1:1 as a bridge between the two books.
